Gateway v2

What. A new version of the egress vision. It adds a second layer for SaaS calls and inbound webhooks. The 1918 page stays as it is for the LLM layer. Answer. The gateway knows no application logic. It makes each provider's API hard to misuse and logs every call and event the same neutral way. Slack goes first. Gmail stays out. Read this if you send to Slack, Zernio, Resend or Stripe, receive their webhooks, or plan the gateway's phases.

1 · The ask

  1. The owner: "i highly confidently want Slack, Zernio integration & webhook here, and also for Resend, Stripe, Gmail to a lower degree. so like it does send_email or crate_stripe same but this stays and orchestrates, forces correct pattern, reliably accepts logs routes webhooks ... doens't need to be big bang though."
  2. Then: "i want a reliable API for these services as they are often so easy to misuse. no this gateway doesn't know application logic, it just forces correct application and does neutral logging understand..?"
  3. Earlier, still in force: "NEVER litellm." The four purposes from the 1918 page also stand: no provider keys in apps, one way to call from any language, one place to watch, routing with fallback for LLMs.
  4. All requests, verbatim, are in requests.html. The evidence files are inv-slack-zernio.md, inv-resend-stripe-gmail.md and provider-retry-policies.md.

2 · First principle: no application logic

  1. The gateway never decides anything for the product. It does not choose who gets an email, what a checkout holds, or what a webhook means. The app decides all of that.
  2. It makes the provider's API hard to misuse. It requires idempotency keys where the provider supports them. It checks every webhook signature. It applies the provider's own timeout, retry, backoff and rate-limit rules in one place.
  3. It speaks the provider's shape. A call is slack chat.postMessage, resend emails.send or stripe checkout.sessions.create, with the provider's own body. There are no product verbs like send_welcome_email.
  4. So the provider's SDK keeps working. The app changes the base URL and the key. stripe-node takes a host option, the Resend SDK reads RESEND_BASE_URL, and Slack's WebClient takes slackApiUrl. Today we use no Slack SDK, and Zernio is one raw fetch helper.
  5. It logs every call and every event the same way. One record holds provider, method or event type, caller, status, attempts, latency, units, provider ids and the idempotency key. It holds no secrets and no outbound bodies.
  6. Webhooks are routed by provider, env tag and event type only. The app gets the raw verified bytes and decides what they mean.
  7. The test. A repo-invariant test in apps/egress fails when gateway code imports product code, or when it reads a payload field that is not on the per-provider allowlist (event id, event type, created time, env tag). A second test sends each provider's sample events through and checks that the bytes the app gets equal the bytes the provider sent.

3 · Two layers, one door

  1. Layer 1, LLM proxy. As in the 1918 page. It maps a call type to a model, tries CLIProxyAPI first, uses a paid fallback only where a row allows it, and never retries. It is stateless and never touches the database.
  2. Layer 2, integration proxy. It forwards allowlisted provider methods and adds the provider's rules. A method that is not on the list gets 404. It also runs the webhook receiver.
  3. Both layers forward and never translate. Layer 2 adds headers, checks, waits and a log record. It never converts one provider's format to another's.
  4. Retries are declared, not hidden. Layer 2 retries only rows that are safe to retry: a call with an idempotency key, or a 429 with Retry-After. Every attempt shows in the log. Layer 1 keeps zero retries.
  5. The gateway waits only inside the caller's deadline. The caller sends x-gateway-deadline-ms (default 10,000). If Slack asks for a 30 s wait, the gateway answers 429 with Retry-After instead of hanging.
  6. Layer 2 needs a small store. One Postgres with two tables: inbound_events (raw webhooks) and idempotency_records (24 h answers for providers with no native key, Slack today). This replaces the 1918 rule "No state" for layer 2 only.
  7. One codebase, two Railway services. egress-llm and egress-int run the same image with a different role. A flood of LLM streams or a bad routing-row deploy cannot slow a webhook ack.

5 · Misuse traps the gateway closes

  1. Slack, 9 traps in code. 4 senders have no timeout. 7 ignore 429 Retry-After. digest.py:512 crashes on a 429. User text goes into mrkdwn unescaped on 3 builders, 2 on public forms, so a visitor can type <!channel>. Slack returns HTTP 200 with ok: false. chat.postMessage has no idempotency key.
  2. The gateway closes them this way. It sets a 10 s timeout. It honours Retry-After inside the caller's deadline. It paces each channel to 1 post per second. It logs ok: false as a failure. It rejects <!channel>, <!here> and <!everyone> unless the row allows a broadcast. It answers a repeated idempotency key from idempotency_records for 24 h.
  3. Zernio, 8 traps in code. The helper has no timeout, no retry and no 429 handling. 3 billable POSTs (inbox.ts:639, templates.ts:333, connect.ts:60) send no Idempotency-Key. The webhook writes its dedupe row before the work, so a failed apply loses the event. The raw event is not kept. The signature has no timestamp.
  4. The gateway closes them this way. It sets a timeout. It honours Retry-After within Zernio's 60, 600 or 1,200 rpm tier. It rejects a POST with no Idempotency-Key. It treats a 207 as a partial failure in the log. It stores the raw event and keeps dispatching until the app answers 2xx. It keeps event-id dedupe for 30 days, matching Zernio's redeliver window.
  5. Resend, 10 traps in code. 6 of 7 send sites send no Idempotency-Key. The one keyed site makes a new key per attempt (scheduler.ts:242), so a lost answer can send twice. 4 fetch sites have no timeout. The 650 ms pacer is per isolate, not per account. The inbound hop fails open, has no svix-id dedupe, can do 12 s of work before the ack, and acks events it then loses.
  6. The gateway closes them this way. It rejects a send with no Idempotency-Key. It sets a 15 s timeout. It paces the whole account to Resend's 10 requests per second. It fails closed on a missing secret. It dedupes on svix-id. It acks right after the insert. It stores an unparseable body as a dead letter instead of returning 500 forever.
  7. The gateway cannot judge a key's quality. A key per attempt still passes the check. The phase that moves Resend sends also changes the key to one per message. The same holds for Stripe's 30 s window key in autoReplenishAction.ts:28.
  8. Stripe, 8 traps in code. 31 mutating SDK calls carry no app key, including 6 creates and 2 invoices.pay. The SDK's own key covers only its retries inside one call. apps/search and api-portal use the 80 s SDK timeout, and api-portal pins no API version. Two receivers process before the ack with no event-id dedupe.
  9. The gateway closes them this way. It rejects a POST whose key is missing or is the SDK's automatic stripe-node-retry- key. It sets a 20 s timeout. It pins Stripe-Version per row. It retries 429 and 5xx with backoff and the same key. It runs one receiver that stores before it acks, with a 300 s tolerance on the raw bytes.
  10. Gmail, 6 traps in code. The send has no idempotency and is retried. 5 calls have no timeout. invalid_grant looks like a network error. These stay app fixes, because Gmail stays out of the gateway.

7 · Inbound webhooks

  1. Public ingress. One HTTPS URL per provider per env, for example https://int.egress.virev.ai/in/stripe. Register only https://. Railway turns a POST to http:// into a GET and drops the body.
  2. Verify first, on raw bytes. Stripe t=,v1=, Svix v1, over id.ts.body, Slack v0= over v0:ts:body, Zernio hex over the body. Timestamp tolerance is 300 s where the provider signs a timestamp. A bad signature gets 400 and a counted reject, never a stored row.
  3. Store before ack. Insert into inbound_events (provider, event id, env tag, type, headers, raw body, received at). A unique index on (provider, event id) is the dedupe. Commit, then answer 2xx. The whole path has a 1 s budget, inside Slack's 3 s.
  4. A repeat is acked and dropped. A unique-index hit answers 200 and logs a duplicate.
  5. Route by table. One row per (provider, env tag, event type) names the app route, for example Convex /in/stripe. An unknown type is stored as unrouted and still acked, so no provider disables the endpoint.
  6. Dispatch. A worker sends the raw bytes, the original provider headers and an x-gateway-signature HMAC. The app checks one scheme instead of four. A 2xx means the app accepted the event.
  7. Retry and dead letter. Dispatch retries at 10 s, 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 6 h and 12 h. After that the row is dead, and the Egress board alerts on any dead row.
  8. Replay. An ops-key endpoint sets rows back to pending by id, provider or time range. The app must accept a repeat, which every current handler already does by event id.
  9. Retention. Raw bodies are kept 30 days, then deleted. That matches the longest provider replay window (Stripe and Zernio).

  1. When the gateway is down, the provider's own retry is the fallback. A gateway or Postgres failure answers 503 or times out. Every provider then retries for 6 minutes to 3 days, and four of five can replay later.
  2. Stripe keeps a documented direct path. The Convex /stripe-webhook route stays deployed. The runbook adds it as a Stripe endpoint if the gateway is down for more than 1 hour. The events.list sweep closes any gap.

8 · Placement: Railway, confirmed

  1. Railway, next to CLIProxyAPI. Inbound needs a public HTTPS edge and restarts we do not run by hand. Railway gives both. The 1918 reasons for layer 1 still hold.
  2. The setup. 2 replicas per service. A healthcheck path. Overlap and draining seconds set. Serverless off, because a slept service can answer 502. No volume on the gateway, because a volume means downtime on every deploy.
  3. Postgres is a separate Railway service. It has a volume, so a Postgres redeploy causes a short outage. During it the receiver answers 503 and providers retry.
  4. Not us-metal01. It went dark on 2026-10-08 from 17:06Z to 17:27Z. That is longer than Slack's 6 min retry tail.
  5. Not Convex. Convex is public and highly available and already hosts 4 receivers. It is the product layer, though, and the gateway must stay neutral. Convex stays the Stripe fallback.
  6. The risk we accept. Railway has no SLA below Business Class. Its status page showed 99.98% uptime per region over 90 days on 2026-10-09. Provider retry tails cover outages shorter than 6 minutes for Slack and 27 hours for the rest.

9 · Constraints added or changed

  1. No application logic in the gateway. Tested as in item 11. A row may name a provider method, a timeout, a retry rule, a pacing rule and a route. It may not name a product concept.
  2. Never translate, in both layers. The 1918 rule now covers layer 2 too.
  3. Idempotency is required where the provider supports it. Stripe, Resend and Zernio POSTs without a key get 400 and reach no provider.
  4. Every webhook is verified, stored, then acked. No receiver does product work before the ack.
  5. Layer 1 never touches the database. A Postgres outage cannot stop an LLM call.
  6. Bodies. Outbound bodies are never stored. Raw inbound bodies are stored 30 days, readable only with the ops key.
  7. Ops alerts stay direct. As in the 1918 page.
  8. Each move deletes the old path. When Slack moves, the 8 copies go. When the Resend receiver moves, the SvelteKit route goes. When Resend sends move, the idle component goes.

10 · Phases

  1. Phase 0, subtract first. Check which Stripe receivers the dashboard calls and delete the others. Remove RESEND_API_KEY from research-agent-be and the Stripe keys from research-app. Make the Resend hop fail closed.
    Staging: one Stripe test event is processed by exactly 1 webhook route.
  2. Phase 1, the service and Slack. Build apps/egress with the row table, the neutral log, the ops key and the idempotency store. Add the Slack rows. Move the 7 product senders. Delete the 8 copies. Land the neutrality test.
    Staging: two Slack posts sent with the same idempotency key show as 1 message in the channel.
  3. Phase 2, the receiver with Resend. Build verify, store, ack, dispatch, retry, dead letter and replay. Point Resend at the gateway. Delete the apps/search webhook route.
    Staging: with Convex refusing Resend events for 10 minutes, all 20 test events land once after it recovers.
  4. Phase 3, Zernio. Add the Zernio call rows and the receiver row. Move ZERNIO_API_KEY to the gateway only. Route by profile env tag.
    Staging: a Zernio inbox send without an Idempotency-Key gets 400 and reaches no Zernio API.
  5. Phase 4, Resend sends. Move the 17 sites. Use one key per message. Remove @convex-dev/resend and keep status in searchEmailMessages.
    Staging: one campaign email sent twice with the same idempotency key arrives once.
  6. Phase 5, Stripe webhooks. Point Stripe at the gateway, forwarding to the Convex ledger. Write the fallback runbook.
    Staging: with the gateway stopped for 30 minutes, every Stripe test event from that window lands in Convex once.
  7. Phase 6, Stripe API. Only after 30 days of phase 5 with no dead rows. Set the SDK host in the 3 clients. Add app keys to the 31 unkeyed mutating calls.
    Staging: a Stripe create call with no app idempotency key gets 400 and reaches no Stripe API.
  8. Track L, LLM layer. Runs in parallel, as in the 1918 page, with its own criteria.

11 · Where this differs from the ops chat's opinion

  1. No product verbs. The opinion named send_slack, send_email and create_checkout. This page uses the provider's own methods, so the gateway holds no product words and SDKs keep working. The owner's second message points the same way.
  2. "Never translates" holds for both layers. The opinion kept it for layer 1 only. Layer 2 needs no translation either. It adds rules and leaves the body alone.
  3. Slack has 7 movable senders, not 9. There are 10 code sites. The 3 ops scripts and 4 Grafana receivers stay direct. The win is timeouts, 429 handling and escaping, not fewer keys. SLACK_BOT_TOKEN_DEV keeps its Grafana and watch holders.
  4. The receiver starts with Resend, not Zernio. Resend already crosses an apps/search hop, so the gateway replaces a hop. Zernio's receiver is the healthiest today, and moving it first adds a hop. Zernio comes one phase later.
  5. The Resend component does not queue for us. Its queue, retries and rate limiter never run. We call it only for status rows. So remove it in phase 4. There is nothing to weigh keeping.
  6. Slack webhooks have no consumer yet. There are 0 Slack inbound routes. Build one only when a feature needs it, with Delayed Events on.
  7. Two services, not one. Same code and image. The LLM layer and the receiver have different load and must fail apart.
  8. Agreed as proposed. Stripe keys pass through, Stripe stores before it acks with a direct fallback, and Gmail stays out.
